thread:
Jordan: Heads up — need final Q1 procurement commit by EOD Friday. Product is pushing for an EU dedicated pool for 2 enterprise customers (est ~200k tokens/day each). Lead time for H100-style units is currently ~12–14 weeks. Can we do a partial reserve (reserve some H100s, more A100s) + spot overlay for burst?
Maria: Clarify SLA: are we promising latency SLO or just capacity/uptime?
Jordan: Product expects 99.9% uptime for dedicated pools. Latency SLOs: p50 ~150ms, p95 target depends on model; key ask is predictable throughput for bursty chat.
Asha: From Product: EU isolation is a must for both customers. They'll pay a premium. They can accept small cold starts if we document them and provide warmup plan.
Sam: Quick numbers — if we reserve `8 H100 + 12 A100` in eu-west1, rough monthly commit hits finance for approval. Need to confirm exact SKUs and pricing. Any cheaper mixes that still meet perf?
Lee: Ops prefers more A100s for cost predictability; H100s should be for the top-tier customer only. Suggest burst fallback to hosted pool in a different region if cross-region routing is allowed.
Jordan: Cross-region fallback is NOT allowed for EU-only contracts. So fallback only within EU (or hosted EU). That constrains options.
Maria: Proposed options:
- Option A: Reserve `8 H100 + 16 A100` in eu-west1 (more headroom)
- Option B: Reserve `4 H100 + 24 A100` + spot overlay for 30% of capacity (cheaper, more complex)
Which do we prefer?
Asha: Product prefers Option B if we can guarantee a canary route to reserved nodes first and a documented cold-start SLA.
Sam: My vote: Option B + 10% reserved burst buffer to cover initial warmups.
Lee: +1 for B; add prewarmed containers during peak business hours and a simple auto-scale cooldown.
Jordan: OpsBot: `procurement-estimate --quarter Q1-2026 --eu eu-west1 --mix 4H100-24A100`
OpsBot: procurement-estimate: est_commit_cost=$1.2M/month, lead_time=12 weeks, spot_savings~25% — see artifact: https://redwood.internal/procure/1951234567 (reaction :chart_with_upwards_trend:)
Maria: Need rollout and launch criteria documented before procurement: 1) 5% canary traffic for 72h, 2) latency p50/p95 within SLO on canary, 3) billing/usage pipeline validated against sample customers, 4) runbook + pager steps tested.
Asha: I'll own canary tests and prompt sets. Will deliver test suite by Wed.
Sam: I'll finalize SKU list and put a finance ask together by Thu EOD.
Jordan: If procurement slips, fallback policy: automatic reroute to hosted EU pool + notify affected customers via status page and SRE on-call.
Lee: I'll draft the capacity degradation runbook and escalation matrix.
Maria: Decision leaning to Option B with the 10% buffer. Jordan/Sam/Asha — please open procurement ticket and PRD today so we can hit the lead times.
Jordan: Opening PRD + procurement ticket now: ticket #PROC-2026-87. Attaching initial cost sheet.
Sam: Noted — will attach finance approval once done.
Asha: Thanks — I'll start the canary prompts and coordinate with QA.
Lee: Adding runbook to the ticket and tagging on-call.
Maria: Great. Thanks everyone. Final call at 3pm if any objections.
Sam: :thumbsup:
